claims.statement: For uniform x in [0,r), input Q=[x]P for the fixed standard secp256k1 generator P, recover x: the Pollard rho algorithm over order-6 automorphism equivalence classes (negation and GLV endomorphism) with distinguished points in proof.md, revised in v4 with a doubling step function G(R) = canon(2R + S_{j(R)}) whose linear coefficient 2*tau lies outside the order-6 group mu, so that automatic cycles of every length up to the trail cap 2^30 are excluded exactly via ord_r(2) = (r-1)/2^6 (proof.md Sections 6.2-6.3), together with an enforced bounded-retry treatment of exceptional steps and split-coordinate scalar bookkeeping under a specified 24-step rebalancing schedule, succeeds with probability at least 0.405 using at most 2^128.05 total target-group-operation equivalents, including preprocessing, all trials and failures, distinguished-point handling and verification. Peak memory is at most 2^113 bytes; preprocessing is at most 2^27 target-group-operation equivalents and is included in total work; nonuniform advice is at most 2^0 bytes and is included in memory. This is a classical cold attack with no uncharged advice or quantum steps. The success bound relies on the disclosed random-mapping heuristic H1 stated in claim.json and proof.md, narrowed in v4 to collision statistics and per-step uniformity, with the walk's automatic-cycle structure proved separately in proof.md Sections 6.2-6.3, the residual coincidence cycles counted in Section 6.4, and both supported by the included toy experiment at its stated scope; every other step of the argument is exact. The exponential memory is required. This is an analytic attack estimate under the fixed cost model, not an executed production attack.

experiments.purpose: Run the v4 production step function of proof.md (order-6 GLV automorphism classes, canonical representatives by the single-multiplication method with brute-force cross-checks, doubling step, bounded exceptional retries, distinguished-point trails, split-coordinate scalar bookkeeping under the 24-step rebalancing schedule with split-evaluated reports, collision solving) on the toy curve y^2=x^3+11 over F_786433 with prime group order 784897 (130817 classes, ord(2)=196224, ell_min=32704, both computed and reported by the program; the v2/v3 toy subgroup 262657 has ord(2)=27 and cannot model the v4 mechanism). The initial (declared) run is the doubling attack configuration: steps-metric success 0.600 against the 0.405 target the budget rule (exponent 0.519195) encodes, visited-metric 0.390, mean visited 447.7 vs 453.3 predicted, trapped trails 4, affected steps 1, total group operations 203516, 237605 split-state invariant checks and 135847 canonicalisation cross-checks with zero violations. Suggested follow-up inputs within the schema: (a) walk='plain' with otherwise identical inputs (the control: steps-metric 0.420, trapped trails 485, total operations 131972, isolating the doubling step's effect); (b) mode='census' with walk='plain' and walk='doubling' at J=32 and also at J=16, 64, 128 (trials=1): exact functional-graph censuses whose plain two-cycle states track N''/(6J) (1430/620/352/192 vs 1363/681/341/170 predicted) while the doubling walk's are 0/2/0/2 and its total cyclic states (412/465/552/156) sit at the random-mapping scale sqrt(pi N/2) ~ 453; (c) mode='census', walk='doubling', J=32, seed=777 (independent table: 281 cyclic states, 0 two-cycle states); (d) mode='census', walk='bumped', J=32, seed=20261106 (the v3 step on this curve: 721 cyclic states, 0 two-cycle states, longest cycle 711 -- healthy at toy scale, as in v3; its production failure is the counting argument of proof.md Section 6.1, not visible to any toy census). This does not establish production curve behavior, production probabilities, memory bounds, or operation costs.

title: secp256k1-ecdlp: Pollard rho over GLV automorphism equivalence classes with a doubling step function (v4)
